caption: How a spot is checked: the game tints the range circle red where a tower cannot stand (left, on the track) and grey where it can (right).
The first track map, made by watching bloons move in a real game: blue near the entrance, red near the exit. Patchy, with whole stretches missing.
An early placement scan on a coarse grid: green where towers may stand, the coloured band around the track ruled out. Blocky, and every probe cost time.
An early win on Easy, saved while teaching the bot to recognise the victory screen and move on to the next game.
The HUD the bot reads every second. OCR sometimes saw phantom digits in the cash, so it now takes the lower median of three reads.
Locked map cards say 'click to unlock', and the bot took them for the tower-choice carousel. It now needs the words 'choose a monkey' first.
The tower-choice carousel offering a single tower, Spike Factory. Instead of circling for more, the bot now takes the only offer after one lap.
Heat maps after more games on Logs, Bloonarius Prime and Monkey Meadow. Meadow is nearly empty: bloons popped near the entrance never showed the rest of the track.
A high-level account: Dart Monkey with 773,006 tower XP and the Apex Plasma Master paragon. The account sync had to learn to read trees like this.
Mode medals on a map card, zoomed in: one badge per difficulty and mode. The bot now reads them for every map in one sweep of the map pages.
The Hard mode screen. Sub-modes are now started by their fixed button slots, and the Sandbox button is never pressed by mistake.
Eight maps' learned tracks side by side, frames watched in the corner. Broken lanes, scenery noise and missing loops: not good enough to place towers by.
The fix: learn each map in Sandbox, where rounds can be sent with no towers on the map, so the bloons run the whole track.
First Sandbox pass on Monkey Meadow. The movement masks (right) caught bats and swaying scenery as speckles, so the background had to be learned first.
Monkey Meadow learned in Sandbox: the whole figure-eight, from the entrance (blue) to the exit (red), in one clean pass.
Bloonarius Prime in Sandbox: only scattered strokes of the track lit up. Some maps would not give up their track this way.
On a darker map the frame differences (right) light up big patches of scenery instead of the thin trail of bloons.
Next step: read the maps from the game's own files. Spice Islands, Logs and Infernal come out exact, with no game played; the fourth map is still a tangle.
Luminous Cove's paths drawn flat over a real game miss the raised loops where the bloons are: the camera is tilted and these paths have height.
The Advanced maps page: locked cards and the category's unlock bar. The medal sweep now reads that bar to know how close the next map is.
Tree Stump's path as the file stores it: numbered control points. Joined with straight lines they cut across the spiral; the game draws smooth curves through them.
Paths built the way the game builds them (Bezier chains and splines) now sit on the track, on Tree Stump and Monkey Meadow alike.
Placement from the game's own area data on Tree Stump: green where a Dart Monkey fits, red for track, trees and the stump. No probing needed.
Checking the camera height factor k on map pictures: Luminous Cove at k=0 and 0.5, Ancient Portal at k=0 and 0.6. The edges agreed with the live-bloon fit, 0.55.
Logs: the grass blocks between the lanes are holes in the track area. Read as holes (yellow), the best tower ground was usable again.
First frame of the rolling screen recording, with the bot's status strip on top. Every game since can be cut into clips like the ones in this video.
A full-run video: a whole game sped up four times, with captions for each tower and the bot build that played it.
Every Monkey Knowledge page in one sheet. Learned nodes are remembered now instead of being checked again every session.
The hero picker, opened by the calibration probe: portraits on the left, the selected hero's details in the middle.
The hero list before and after one scroll, used to measure how far a scroll moves the portraits.
Silhouette masks cut from hero portraits: too patchy to tell heroes apart, so the picker reads the name each portrait shows instead.
One medal sweep, every map page in one sheet. Medals earned outside the usual unlock order are kept now: they are real co-op medals.
Round 47 on Luminous Cove: the bloons pile up on the raised loops at the top, where no tower reaches, and 56 lives go at once.
The Double Cash and Fast Track toggles beside the hero button. The bot reads them now, and the planner counts the extra cash when it rates its chances.
The lost game with the bot's projected paths (yellow, red): bloons run the top loops, but every tower (white circles) sat at the bottom. Placement is being fixed for this.
A Collection Event screen that appeared between games and confused the bot's way back to the menus.
Collection event crate: face-down reward cards on black and almost no text, which the bot first read as an unknown screen and got stuck on.
Why Luminous Cove was lost: white dots are every spot a ninja may stand - only the rock at the bottom. Most of the track (green to red) is out of land towers' reach.
Deflation's intro box sat over the game; the bot saw the HUD, thought it was playing and could not pick up a single tower.
